name: New Mexico Environment Department and Office of the State Engineer
program: Strategic Water Supply Program grants and contracts (brackish water research, design pilots, demonstration)
collect_note: The program's own pages (env.nm.gov) return HTTP 503 to plain fetch and to headless Chrome, so the crawler reads the program's Submittable portal (nmose.submittable.com/submit), the only application route, which is server-rendered and lists each open call as a /submit/<guid> link; it keeps those links and hops to each call page for a deadline. The funder page is fetched second for text and a failure there is ignored. Calls wait as hidden candidates for review.

zero_reason.quote: There are presently no open calls for submissions.

evidence: 2026-11-13: env.nm.gov/strategic-water-supply/ (grant page, contracts page, how-to-apply, /requests-for-proposals/, robots.txt, sitemap_index.xml, wp-json/wp/v2/pages/19, /feed/) all HTTP 503 (plain curl, fetch_text, headless Chrome via endpoint_recon); env.nm.gov without www fails TLS hostname check; ose.nm.gov times out. Wayback capture of the grant page 2026-09-19 names the Submittable portal https://nmose.submittable.com/submit (200 over plain HTTP, 7971 chars of text, no sitemap, no feed; endpoint_recon verdict html_ok, only Submittable's own org JSON /api/organizations/<guid> which holds the same portal description, not a call list). Portal now reads 'There are presently no open calls for submissions.' (the 2026 round closed 2026-10-20), so zero items today; the link pattern /submit/<guid> is Submittable's standard call link and could not be tested on a live open call. No past call title exists on the portal to test the filter against.
